claim: With no BAR1-P2P driver patches, cuDeviceCanAccessPeer is 0 on all six ordered pairs of three cards, so the driver stages every GPU-to-GPU copy through host memory at 6.21-6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB (single-card D2H 6.68 GB/s) and 22 us at 4 KiB, identical same-switch and cross-switch.
stance_target: the repo's 'no P2P' premise in the default unlocked configuration, and the host-staged bandwidth ceiling that any all-reduce on this box inherits
scope_conditions: Three memory-unlocked cards at Gen2 x16, two behind one PLX PEX 8747 switch and one behind a second, bare metal, no BAR1-P2P patches; measured 2026-10-01
quoted_support: `cuDeviceCanAccessPeer` is 0 on all six ordered pairs, so the driver stages every GPU-to-GPU copy through host memory: 6.21–6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB (single-card D2H 6.68 GB/s), 22 µs at 4 KiB, identical same-switch and cross-switch.

claim: NCCL falls back to SHM on this fabric and a two-GPU all-reduce reaches 3.69 GB/s (same switch) and 3.85 GB/s (cross switch) bus bandwidth at 256 MiB, with 120-145 us at 8 KiB.
stance_target: the measured all-reduce bandwidth that DDP gradient reduction would actually get on this box — the single most load-bearing number for the repo's DDP-feasibility arithmetic
scope_conditions: Three cards at Gen2 x16 behind PLX switches, no BAR1-P2P, NCCL SHM transport, 256 MiB and 8 KiB message sizes
quoted_support: NCCL picks SHM: two-GPU all-reduce 3.69 GB/s (same switch) and 3.85 GB/s (cross switch) bus bandwidth at 256 MiB, 120–145 µs at 8 KiB.

claim: Tensor parallelism is link-bound on this fabric: when one card's link retrained from x8 to x1, TP4 fell from 70.5 to 14.4 tok/s under an unchanged protocol while PP4 held 60.8 tok/s on the same box — about 4.2x more link-tolerant.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is a viable topology on a degraded PCIe fabric; a single bad rank collapses TP throughput by ~4.9x while PP is nearly unaffected
scope_conditions: Four-card CMP 170HX, GLM-5.3-Flash, one card retrained x8 -> x1, unchanged protocol, same box
quoted_support: TP is link-bound on this fabric: with no NVLink, every all-reduce crosses PCIe and the topology runs at the width of its worst rank. When one card's link retrained from x8 to x1, TP4 fell from 70.5 to 14.4 tok/s under an unchanged protocol while PP4 held 60.8 tok/s on the same box — about 4.2x more link-tolerant.

claim: Doubling the PCIe link rate does not move pipeline-parallel decode: MiMo-V2.6-Flash PP3 ran 74.6 tok/s at Gen2 x16 versus 75.5 tok/s at Gen1 x16.
stance_target: the claim that PP's cost is dominated by per-stage compute and HBM bandwidth rather than the interconnect, which is what makes PP viable on a slow fabric
scope_conditions: Three-card CMP 170HX, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL PP3, vLLM sm80 image, 180 W, behind PLX switches, no P2P
quoted_support: P1 greedy c=1: PP3 74.6 (prior 75.5), PP3 + MTP k=2 113.8 (117.7) tok/s ... Doubling the link rate does not move PP decode.

claim: TP2 without P2P buys single-stream latency and 2.5x the KV cache but not throughput: Qwen3.8-27B decode 54.0 tok/s at TP1 versus 72.0 at TP2, prefill 1,914 versus 1,695-1,736 tok/s at 6,603 tokens, and aggregate at c=16 546 versus 530-535.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is a throughput win on this fabric — it is a latency and capacity play, and it costs prefill and aggregate throughput
scope_conditions: dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound, club SM80 vLLM image, 180 W, Gen2 x16 behind PLX switches, no P2P (NCCL SHM), prefix cache off
quoted_support: Decode256: TP1 54.0, TP2 72.0 (same switch) / 71.9 (cross switch), TP2 + MTP k=3 103.5 tok/s. Prefill at 6,603 tokens: 1,914 (TP1) vs 1,695–1,736 (TP2) tok/s. Aggregate at c=16: 546 (TP1), 530–535 (TP2), 385 (TP2 + MTP). TP2 buys single-stream latency and 2.5x the KV cache, not throughput.

claim: A four-card CMP 170HX rig at c=8 serves DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp at 220 tok/s for about $0.90 per million output tokens, versus two DGX Spark nodes at 81 tok/s for about $2.13 per million, but the Spark nodes win on energy at 3,172 versus 1,457 tok/Wh.
stance_target: the cost-per-token case for running experiments on this box rather than an alternative platform
scope_conditions: Same checkpoint and protocol on both platforms; hardware prices, electricity rate and a three-year/50%-utilization lifetime are chosen inputs, not measurements; throughput and GPU power are measured
quoted_support: At c=8, the CMP rig moves more tokens per second, but the Spark nodes move more tokens per watt-hour. ... Neither number is free of assumptions: hardware prices, electricity rate, and the three-year/50%-utilization lifetime are all inputs we chose, not measurements.

claim: NVFP4 checkpoints are incompatible with SM80 because they are SM121-format weights, and a BF16 fallback of a large model on four cards OOMs above roughly 1,024 input tokens and decodes at only 0.88-0.93 tok/s.
stance_target: the constraint that quantisation and precision choices on this box are limited to W4A16/AWQ/Marlin dequant paths, which bounds which training and inference experiments are runnable
scope_conditions: Three to four CMP 170HX cards, SM80; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp FP8 -> BF16 fallback on the reference TP4 runtime plus SM80 patches
quoted_support: | GLM-5.3-Flash  | NVFP4  | 3  | ... | Not compatible (SM121 weights on SM80)  | ... | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp  | FP8 → BF16 fallback · reference TP4 runtime + SM80 patches  | 4 · TP4  | ≤ ~1,024 input tokens (OOM above)  | batch 1  | 512 tokens in ~8.7–9.8 s  | 0.88–0.93 tok/s

claim: The benchmark index contains no training measurements at all — every row is a serving/decode/prefill benchmark — so it cannot directly validate any training-topology claim.
stance_target: the evidentiary gap in the corpus: hardware-envelope numbers exist for inference only, so training-throughput claims must be derived by arithmetic from inference measurements or from first principles
scope_conditions: Full BENCHMARKS.md normalised matrix, 615 lines, as of 2026-10-02
quoted_support: Results here are application measurements on the tested CMP 170HX setup. They are not vendor specifications or theoretical estimates. This page is the normalized comparison index

claim: A single card's decode throughput is largely insensitive to link generation: a matched SGLang ladder re-run on a Gen1 x4 to Gen2 x4 reseat reproduced every prompt depth within 0.3%.
stance_target: how much of the box's behaviour is fabric-limited — single-card work is not, so fabric cost only appears in multi-card collectives
scope_conditions: One CMP 170HX, SGLang, matched ladder across the link change, 1k-128k depths
quoted_support: PCIe trained at Gen1 x4 (0.84 GB/s) for runs before 2026-09-10, Gen2 x4 (1.69 GB/s) after a reseat. A matched SGLang ladder on the new link reproduced every depth within 0.3%.

claim: The club's PP4 recipe of record at 393,216 configured context delivered 87.6 tok/s c=1 decode and 78.4 tok/s aggregate at c=16 on a degraded link, with 1,128 tok/s prefill at 4k and 1,752 tok/s at 16k.
stance_target: the achievable per-card throughput envelope for a 4-card pipeline-parallel run at long context, useful as a sanity bound on any training-throughput estimate
scope_conditions: GLM-5.3-Flash AWQ W4A16, vLLM sm80, PP4 partition 14,12,12,7 + MTP k=3, 4 cards, 393,216 configured context, 131,042 prompt tokens measured, degraded link
quoted_support: | GLM-5.3-Flash  | AWQ W4A16 (compressed-tensors) · vLLM sm80, PP4 partition 14,12,12,7 + native MTP k=3  | 4 · PP4  | 393,216 configured; 131,042 prompt tokens measured  | c=1/2/4/8/16  | 1,128 tok/s at 4k, 1,752 tok/s at 16k (degraded link)  | 87.6 tok/s (c=1, temp 0, median of 3, clean)
